title: Extend one-command task sync to memory-enabled data branches
outcome: Extend one-command task sync to memory-enabled data branches
acceptance: On an enrolled host whose committed data branch already carries project memories, `engram task-sync sync` performs the full two-way task and memory exchange without the operator issuing separate export or import commands; task-only branch behavior stays unchanged

The one-command route preserves keyed memory revision history, attribution and forget tombstones, reports withheld or partially refused memory outcomes with their remedies, and keeps the existing task conflict/held/refused-import and exact-retry behavior without transferring live claims, delivery state or private scratch

Behavior tests drive the CLI on two enrolled hosts with task and memory changes in both directions, including a forget propagated from one host to the other and an exact repeat after a resolved refusal; existing explicit memory export/import behavior remains covered

Command help, docs/features/git-task-sync.md and docs/skills/engram-use/SKILL.md describe the resulting one-command memory behavior and only the recovery cases that still require explicit commands; the change passes the full required gate and review pair
disposal_reason: Duplicate: Engram::Fable filed w-bd4bfba779a7 at 16:54Z for the same one-command memory sync. Sol 11330 already holds it, and Greg called the gap a bug to fix now (Asistant 43498a6e #2094), so it does not wait behind w-443806ecaf50.
